touches.text: Tool: a complete primitive. Has users, not an owner. Calls no other Cairn component (stdlib and base only) and owns no state of its own. Lives in cairn/tools/ (17). Its data for a holder lives under that holder: ~/.cairn/devices/<device>/<instance>/tools/<tool>/.

Cairn owns all of ~/.cairn/ and delegates each ~/.cairn/devices/ subtree to its device. Everything outside devices/ (~/.cairn/logging/ and the rest) is Cairn's, so every log is Cairn's and Cairn cleans them up in sleep. Transient things are files there; trouble tickets are logging items.

Cairn owns everything about the system that is Cairn and hasn't been delegated elsewhere. A delegated domain belongs to its device, not to Cairn, even though it is of Cairn: the librarian is delegated learning, research and answering queries on what's learned; the embeddings device is delegated producing the embeddings we search with. The OS and hardware belong to Recovery (6.6).
TOOLS (cairn/tools/: the general collection; tools have users, not owners)

Where a tool lives: the general collection, cairn/tools/, is the default. A tool goes with its holder (cairn/devices/<d>/tools/) only when nothing else could ever use it: "if i build a tool for adjusting the farfignator on a vw golf from the 80s, and nothing else in the universe has a farfignator, then it can go with the car." If there is any chance somebody else might want it, it goes in the general collection.

dataref: one address for any stored record, in any format, and the thin class that reads it. Shaped by Akien and CC 2026-11-09, grown from CC0AC-Weather 1.4.8's secrets.env. WHY: a config, a ticket or a node can say WHERE a value lives without carrying it, so the repo stays shareable and a private value stays in ~/.cairn; and one way of pointing works across every format and every box. USERS: anything that reads stored data.

conflicts.ticket_says: writes ~/.cairn/usage/usage.json carrying fetched_at, and keeps a failed fetch beside the last good reading
conflicts.why: Outline 1.3.1 specifies that tools 'own no state of its own' and 'Its data for a holder lives under that holder: ~/.cairn/devices/<device>/<instance>/tools/<tool>/'. The ticket's design writes data to ~/.cairn/usage/, which neither follows the prescribed per-holder nested structure nor specifies which device/instance is the holder. Both storage patterns cannot be true simultaneously: tool data either lives under the device/instance that holds it (per outline), or it lives at ~/.cairn/ level directly (per ticket).
